student_start: Same persistent-student/context/replay implementation and world generator as E17, with 2,304 batches per arm. Fresh stream seeds; no regime IDs or boundary resets. Restore E9 bootstrap procedure for all learned arms. No new reset-student bootstrap.
meta_signal: Keep the starting parameter/moment state and exact training batches of the eight updates immediately preceding the final ordinary batch. Differentiate their replay through the current procedure. Objective is half loss on that next ordinary batch before its update and half loss on 128 previously observed reservoir examples. Every label is already observed before proposing a procedure; none comes from the subsequent trial. The retrospective replay is charged, and its source tensors consume bounded memory.
trial: Copy the current student/moments after ordinary learning into incumbent and candidate branches. Each sees the next sixteen actual batches, predicts before targets, and then updates. Operational errors come from the incumbent for the entire trial, regardless of later admission. The candidate is admitted only when its mean trial error improves by more than 0.1 percent and a fixed pre-trial sample of 128 old observed examples degrades by at most 2 percent against the incumbent endpoint. Adopt the winning current student and moments after the trial, never a reset student. Old-sample guards are finite and may overlap replay training; no held-out retention certificate is claimed.
proposal_control: Both online arms differentiate the same type of retrospective objective, clip meta-gradients to norm one, use the same 0.003 outer rate and Adam moments with accepted-step counting, and have the same trial/admission opportunity. Self-application uses the incumbent controller on gradients of its own parameters; conventional meta-updates use multiplier one. Proposal moments advance only upon admission. Both are compared with frozen bootstrap and fixed Adam at 0.01, with full extra costs.
evaluation: All 48 rounds are reported. Clean prequential errors are evaluation-only, with operational trial predictions fixed to the incumbent. Report first/final quarters, per-round admissions and candidate/incumbent trial errors, all segment boundaries and censored E17 recovery measures. No final-stream labels tune rules, rates, thresholds or checkpoints.
preflight: Verify retrospective replay exactly reproduces the recorded student state before the query update, finite-difference meta-gradient on float64 dummy tensors, first zero-controller self proposal equals conventional update, complete student-state copying and exact operational-incumbent accounting. Check procedure changes cannot use future trial targets. Verify bounded trace and replay sizes and record the test work.
costs: Charge all ordinary and duplicate trial student work, retrospective updates, meta-gradient calls, controller inference including outer self-application, admission scoring, trace/branch/procedure tensor storage and local wall time. Count observations acquired once separately from repeated use. Link E9 bootstrap work. Reuse identical Adam baseline cases across controller replicates with new/inherited work separated. No complete FLOPs, process RAM, energy or fixed-time claim.
falsification: Admission counts alone are not improvement. Online self-application must improve subsequent operational learning over conventional extra meta-training and freezing on both kinds of stream without hiding recovery failures or duplicate work. A failure to beat those controls rejects this concrete recursive mechanism. Gains in this restricted full-feedback setting do not establish closed-loop counterfactual validity, arbitrary architecture invention or open-ended improvement.
scope: First online self-applied procedure with persistent student/optimizer/context/experience in this project. Fixed small controller family, bounded finite trials, two inherited bootstrap replicates and two fresh worlds per family. Not a general reasoning, semantic compression, long-horizon control or research-novelty result.
